 GLD closed at its lowest level since September 2025 as spot gold sank below $3,800, with most of the drop coming after U.S. markets closed. 
 St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy will likely need "several" rate increases before spring 2027, and markets now price hikes in December and January. 
 Goldman Sachs cut its end-2026 gold target to $4,150 from $4,650, yet still sees prices above current levels. 
 Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor) 
 Spot gold slipped below $3,800 an ounce on the evening of Tuesday, November 17, 2026, for the first time since September 2025. At 12:48 a.m. ET Wednesday, November 18, spot traded at $3,790.18, down 1.5%. U.S. gold futures stood at $3,823.67, down 1.1%. 
 Courtesy of Agnico Eagle Mines Limited Silver fell 0.8% to $47.01 and platinum traded at $1,424.45, showing rate-driven selling. Futures confirm the break: after settling at $3,864.20, they hit $3,781.70 and were $3,794.00 at 12:51 a.m. They last closed lower on September 25, 2025, at $3,771.10. 
 Most of the drop came after the U.S. market closed. SPDR Gold Shares ( NYSEARCA:GLD ) ended Tuesday at $352.48, down 0.13%. That was its lowest close since September 29, 2025, so GLD holders will see the overnight loss when trading opens Wednesday. 
 Fed Hike Talk Sent Gold Lower 
 St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem spoke in Argentina on Tuesday. He said the economy will likely need "several" rate increases before spring 2027. He wants the real policy rate (the fed funds rate minus inflation) at 2% to 2.5% by then. That is well above his current estimate.

 Musalem does not vote on policy until 2028. Even so, markets now expect quarter-point hikes in December and January and another by April, starting from the current 3.75% to 4.00% range. ANZ estimates that markets have priced in about 80 basis points of tightening for this cycle. A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point. 
 Story Continues Yields and a Strong Dollar Are Pushing Gold Down 
 Because gold pays no interest, a 10-year Treasury yielding about 5.09% raises the cost of holding gold instead of bonds. 
 The dollar index reached 103.65 overnight, its highest since its April 2, 2025 close. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for buyers who pay in other currencies. 
 Gold has fallen sharply, mostly because of high yields and the strong dollar. Spot sits about 32% below its $5,594.82 record from January 29, 2026. Futures sit about 29% below their $5,318.40 record close. 
 Gold Miners Rose Before the Overnight Drop 
 Newmont ( NYSE:NEM ) rose 0.86% to $111.26 on Tuesday. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF ( NYSEARCA:GDX ) gained 0.79% to $79.57. Over the week, Newmont fell 7.25%, and GDX fell 8%. 
 NEM Price Target — 24/7 Wall St. Miners have high fixed costs, so their profits rise and fall faster than the gold price. This is called operating leverage, and it amplifies losses when gold falls. GDX closed 31.3% below its February 27, 2026 record close. 
 Newmont makes up about 10.4% of GDX. Its stock is up 11.4% this year, helped by $1.9 billion of third-quarter free cash flow. 
 NEM Analyst Ratings — 24/7 Wall St. What Goldman's Lower Targets Mean for GLD 
 Goldman Sachs ( NYSE:GS ) strategists led by Lina Thomas cut their gold targets in a forecast reported November 13. The end-2026 target fell to $4,150 from $4,650, and the end-2027 target fell to $4,800 from $5,400. They expect a December hike and see central bank buying of 60 tonnes a month as support. 
 A firm bullish on gold is cutting its targets but still expects prices above current levels. That outlook depends on central banks continuing to buy and the Fed ending its rate increases early. 
 GLD's recent record is weak. It is down 11.06% this year, even after a 102.64% gain over five years. Meanwhile, a three-month Treasury bill pays 4.33%, income a gold holder gives up. 
 Newmont's cost structure leaves it profitable at lower gold prices. Its full-year all-in sustaining costs, the full cost of running its mines, are forecast at about $1.52 thousand per ounce. That leaves a wide profit margin even with gold at $3,790.18. 
 The Fed releases minutes from its October 27-28 meeting at 2 p.m. ET on November 18, and its next decision comes December 8-9. If spot gold climbs back above $3,800 and the dollar index falls below 103.65 by then, the case that rising rates and a stronger dollar will keep pressing gold lower would weaken considerably.
